s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption of the extremities with a chronic time course
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on the extremities
Erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face
key_facts: No remarkable medical or family history
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa not involved
Normal laboratory tests, including routine blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor
Skin biopsy showed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

shortlist.label: Grover disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of pruritic papules with histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and vacuolar degeneration of the basal cell layer

shortlist.label: Darier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by keratotic papules and histopathological features of dyskeratosis and suprabasal acantholytic dyskeratosis, which aligns with some of the patient's skin biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with keratotic papules and palmoplantar involvement is not always present, making it a plausible diagnosis despite the patient's palms and soles being unaffected

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Can manifest with pruritic, flat-topped papules and histopathological features of basal cell degeneration and a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, which are partially consistent with the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Keratosis punctata
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by multiple, small, keratotic papules, which could align with the patient's clinical presentation of scattered, erythematous, annular papules

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including intensively pruritic papules and the histopathology findings of mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and individual cell dyskeratosis, are consistent with Grover disease, a rare skin disorder characterized by sudden onset of pruritic papules.

rejected.label: Darier disease
rejected.why: Darier disease typically presents with greasy, crusted papules in seborrheic areas and has a stronger familial component, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: Pityriasis rubra pilaris is characterized by orange-red scaling plaques and palmoplantar keratoderma, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Lichen planus typically presents with flat-topped, violaceous papules and can involve the mucous membranes, which is not consistent with this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Keratosis punctata
rejected.why: Keratosis punctata is characterized by multiple small, hyperkeratotic papules on the palms, which is not consistent with the patient's symptoms and lack of palm involvement.
